title: Scoped negative result: partial leaver cells on #1005's word, and the 192-bit coefficient allowance
body:
**No κ claim.** This is a negative result on the obvious next step after #1005: extending its mutable-leaver cells beyond the eight all-K cells. It does not raise κ. Two of the three obstructions will bind any further leaver-style rewrite on this line, so they seem worth recording.

## What was tried

Outside #1005's eight cells, only 16 delivery keys have leaver operands, and only in two of their three blocks. That is why #1005 stopped at eight. Each of these keys uses three face copies and one slot copy.

- **Exact legality model.** A frame fits a target's hyperplane iff every generator is orthogonal to the target's port, and that property is a union under joins. So legality reduces to a few taint bits per register. A layered CP-SAT model over set and taint states finds the circuits.
- **Construction.** A hook in a copy of #1005's constructor applies one circuit template per key and drops freed copies through the helper map, as #1005 does. The constructor's own exact identity check runs unchanged.
- **Port stages.** Moving own-row reads breaks the port stage's alignment of the all-K cells. A construction-side option anchors unmatched gates to their next matched gate. It is a byte-identical no-op on #1005's word, and every variant needed zero frame repairs.

## Results

Per-call profile deltas are measured on the cold-end word against #1005's cell word. κ uses #1005's global profile with ideal rank-48 packing, an upper bound. Bits are the local replay's coefficient bound, which must stay below 192.

| variant | helpers removed | native audit | bits | κ |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| #1005 baseline | 0 | pass | 188 | 0.001671387264390146 |
| one helper + target-to-target gates | 32 | **fail** (zero-frame compensation reads an entering helper) | — | 0.0016827 if it were legal |
| two kept copies, all 16 keys | 16 | pass | 107 | 0.0016650 (loss) |
| one fresh helper, all 16 keys | 32 | pass | **210** | 0.0016702 (loss) |
| one fresh helper, 4567 class | 16 | pass | **203** | 0.0016723 (+0.05 %) |
| one fresh helper, one key | 2 | pass | 187 | 0.0016712 (loss) |

## Obstructions

1. **The packet copies are entering helpers.** After porting they start with arbitrary dirt, and their original readers pre-read them. A kept copy must keep its exact reader set, and no circuit may copy a dirty target into another target. With own rows first and one helper, CP-SAT proves a key infeasible.
2. **Cold-end pairing collapses.** Every target in the eight touched blocks belongs to one of the 16 keys. Using their own-row registers as leavers moves them out of the block frame, so pairing falls from 4 to 0–2 per block. The copies were what kept the own rows inside.
3. **The 192-bit coefficient allowance is nearly used up.** #1005's word already needs 188 bits, reached in the full-frame cleanup of block 4567's scratch. Eight circuits push it to 203 bits and sixteen to 210. Any further leaver mutation on this line will likely hit this bound first.

## Reproduce

```sh
bash research/leaver-partial-cells/reproduce.sh . /tmp/gauge44-pr635 /tmp/leaver-partial-cells
```

The script runs #645's no-triangle base and #1005's cell driver with its pins checked. It then runs the census (byte-identical cell word), the raw-level template checks and all five variants through regroup, HPE, cold44, the native audit, ledgers and the local replay. Finally it prices them into `RESULTS.json`, which matches the committed file. It takes about 45 minutes. A fresh macOS run (Python 3.11) reproduced every row above. The optional circuit search needs ortools; the README gives the command.

Only `research/leaver-partial-cells/` is added. No inherited file changes: the patches are applied to copies under the output directory.

## Scope and credits

These are finite local measurements on #1005's cell word. Prices assume ideal owner packing and omit #1005's later layers. The negative conclusions hold either way, because the legal variants lose or break the 192-bit rule before any layer applies.

Builds on jeremykothe2's #1005 (leaver cells and the k8 chain), icekylinx's #645 and the no-triangle constructors, and the PR635 supplier lineage. Related scope: #651 (delivery-layer rigidity, which assumed helpers were the only scratch), #717 and #595 (format limits).

Prepared by higherbeing with substantial Claude (Anthropic) assistance.
